articles.title: The 2027 COLA estimate just changed — again. But few Americans noticed. 3 moves to make before it’s officially announced
articles.summary: Experts have changed their minds on what they expect the COLA to be. Here’s the latest data, along with some tips on what you can do to prepare.
articles.body:

The annual Social Security cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) can make or break the finances of retirees, as it determines how much benefits will increase to keep pace with inflation.

Since COLAs are very important to beneficiaries, advocacy groups make predictions throughout the year, offering insight into how much extra money (if any) Social Security recipients will collect in the coming year.

A record 45% of central banks plan to grow gold reserves — and many investors are following suit. Get your free gold IRA guide from Priority Gold

Over the course of 2026, the estimates for the 2027 COLA have been all over the place.

At the start of the year, The Senior Citizens League (TSCL), an advocacy group for older Americans, was predicting a 2.5% COLA for 2027 (1) — a smaller raise than the 2.8% COLA awarded for 2026.

Then, economic conditions took an unexpected turn, and inflation ran substantially higher than expected in 2026.

That sudden change is important because the COLA is directly tied to inflation: The rate for the coming year is calculated (2) based on the current year's third-quarter changes in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W).

As inflation remained stubbornly high, TSCL revised its forecast upward throughout the year.

TSCL's forecast peaked at 3.9% (3) in May, while the most recent estimate — the final one before the official COLA announcement on Oct. 14 — is slightly more conservative, projecting a 3.5% benefit bump (4) in 2027.

This would still be the highest increase since 2023, when benefits rose by 8.7% (5).

For many Americans, these shifts in COLA predictions have largely gone unnoticed. In fact, around three-quarters of adults (74%) expressed interest in learning more about how inflation affects their Social Security benefits, according to a 2025 survey (6) conducted by The Harris Poll on behalf of Nationwide.

Meanwhile, research from the Social Security Administration (SSA) suggests that just over one-quarter (27%) of working-age adults understand how Social Security benefits are calculated (7).

Still, although many Americans may not know the finer points of how COLAs are calculated, most retirees (89%) didn't believe their benefits were keeping pace with inflation, according to TSCL's 2026 Senior Survey (8).

articles.title: Presidente Lula, que concorre à reeleição pelo PT, defende manter a atual política de valorização do salário mínimo | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato também defendeu a necessidade de aumentar investimentos em infraestrutura para melhorar o ritmo de crescimento da economia.
articles.summary: Candidato também defendeu a necessidade de aumentar investimentos em infraestrutura para melhorar o ritmo de crescimento da economia.
articles.body:
O Jornal Nacional mostrou como foi o dia de campanha dos dois candidatos à Presidência da República nesta quinta-feira (8). O presidente Lula , que concorre à reeleição pelo PT , defendeu manter a atual política de valorização do salário mínimo.

A agenda de Lula começou cedo no Palácio da Alvorada com várias reuniões. Primeiro, chegaram integrantes da equipe responsável pela estratégia da campanha. Entre eles, o governador reeleito do Piauí, Rafael Fonteles, do PT, escolhido para coordenar a comunicação nesse segundo turno. Depois, se reuniu com o secretário de Comunicação Social da Presidência, Sidônio Palmeira, e com o ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan.

O presidente da Câmara, Hugo Motta, também se reuniu com Lula. Ele ficou por uma hora no Alvorada. No primeiro turno, o presidente da Câmara apoiou Lula na Paraíba. No escritório de campanha, Lula defendeu a necessidade de aumentar investimentos em infraestrutura para melhorar o ritmo de crescimento da economia:

"A única chance da gente fazer com que a dívida diminua, efetivamente, é você gastar em coisas que são necessárias para o país. Você fazer investimento em ativos que significam aumento de patrimônio desse país: uma ferrovia, uma hidrelétrica, uma rodovia. E, ao mesmo tempo, você fazer a economia crescer com muito investimento em obras de infraestrutura. E isso nós sabemos fazer".

Presidente Lula, que concorre à reeleição pelo PT, defende manter a atual política de valorização do salário mínimo — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

O candidato à reeleição falou em manter a política de valorização do salário mínimo atrelada ao crescimento da economia:

"Por que que o aumento? Porque o PIB, o resultado do crescimento da riqueza produzida por você, por mim e por 215 milhões de habitantes. É justo que, quando a economia cresça 2% ou 3%, e você pega esse crescimento do PIB e reparta para os trabalhadores. E os aposentados continuam sendo trabalhadores".

A coordenação de campanha de Lula fechou a agenda dos primeiros atos de rua no segundo turno, com foco no Nordeste e no Sudeste.

articles.title: 'Imposto do pecado': discussão sobre alíquotas ficará para depois das eleições, diz ministro da Fazenda | G1
articles.standfirst: Tributo, criado pela reforma tributária, será cobrado sobre produtos e serviços considerados prejudiciais à saúde ou ao meio ambiente.
articles.summary: Tributo, criado pela reforma tributária, será cobrado sobre produtos e serviços considerados prejudiciais à saúde ou ao meio ambiente.
articles.body:
Cigarro aumenta vulnerabilidade a infecções — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

O ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, afirmou nesta quinta-feira (8) que as alíquotas do Imposto Seletivo, conhecido como "imposto do pecado", só começarão a ser discutidas após as eleições, quando quando governo enviará ao Congresso Nacional os termos do acordo fechado com os setores afetados.

"A gente concluiu o acordo essa semana e na próxima semana vai ter uma reunião, com o compromisso do governo do presidente Lula de encaminhar o acordo feito com os setores", afirmou o ministro da Fazenda.

O imposto seletivo foi criado pela reforma tributária. O tributo será cobrado sobre produtos e serviços considerados prejudiciais à saúde ou ao meio ambiente.

A ideia é, além de arrecadar, desestimular o consumo desses itens.

A lista de produtos taxados inclui bebidas alcoólicas, refrigerantes e cigarros. O novo imposto também vai incidir sobre alguns veículos, conforme o nível de poluição, sobre a extração de bens minerais.

Como mostrou o g1 , a expectativa da equipe econômica é de arrecadar R$ 41,9 bilhões com o imposto seletivo em 2027 .

️Segundo o Ministério da Fazenda, a ideia é manter a carga tributária que incide sobre os produtos em um período de transição, cujo prazo não foi especificado.

Em um segundo momento, porém, a estratégia é aumentar a taxação "pelo seu efeito regulatório de reduzir o consumo de produtos danosos à saúde e ao meio ambiente".

Junto com a Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS), outro tributo da reforma tributária sobre o consumo que terá início em 2027, o governo busca manter a arrecadação estável em relação ao Produto Interno Bruto (PIB).

articles.title: Endividamento das familias cai; inadimplência sobe na alta renda | G1
articles.standfirst: Inadimplência caiu de 38,8% para 38,5% entre famílias que ganham até 3 salários mínimos, mas subiu de 14,9% para 15% entre aquelas com renda acima de 10 salários.
articles.summary: Inadimplência caiu de 38,8% para 38,5% entre famílias que ganham até 3 salários mínimos, mas subiu de 14,9% para 15% entre aquelas com renda acima de 10 salários.
articles.body:
O endividamento das famílias brasileiras caiu pela primeira vez desde dezembro de 2025. A parcela de famílias com dívidas teve um recuo tímido, passando de 82% em agosto para 81,7% em setembro, segundo a Pesquisa de Endividamento e Inadimplência do Consumidor (Peic), da Confederação Nacional do Comércio de Bens, Serviços e Turismo (CNC).

No mesmo período, a inadimplência recuou entre as famílias que ganham até 3 salários mínimos e aumentou entre aquelas com renda acima de 10 salários mínimos, a única das quatro faixas de renda analisadas em que o indicador subiu.

O indicador vinha em trajetória de alta desde dezembro do ano passado, quando estava em 80,9%. A sequência de aumentos levou o endividamento ao pico de 82,2% em abril e maio.

A expectativa da CNC é que o endividamento das famílias termine o ano relativamente estável, em torno de 81,5%.

Gráfico mostra evolução do endividamento das familias brasileiras — Foto: g1

Qual a diferença entre endividamento e inadimplência?

Endividamento: Ter dívidas não significa necessariamente estar com problemas financeiros. O indicador mede a parcela de famílias que possuem algum compromisso financeiro a vencer, como cartão de crédito, financiamento, empréstimo pessoal, cheque especial ou carnê de loja. Uma pessoa que parcela uma compra no cartão ou paga um financiamento em dia, por exemplo, entra na estatística de endividamento.

Inadimplência: Já a inadimplência indica quando a dívida não foi paga no prazo combinado. Ou seja, são consumidores com contas vencidas e em atraso. Uma família pode estar endividada e não ser inadimplente, caso esteja pagando as parcelas normalmente. Por outro lado, quem deixa uma dívida vencer passa a fazer parte do grupo de inadimplentes.

Inadimplência recua, mas dívidas ficam mais tempo em atraso

A parcela de famílias com dívidas em atraso caiu de 29,9% em agosto para 29,6% em setembro. O resultado também foi melhor que o registrado um ano antes, quando 30,5% das famílias estavam inadimplentes.

O percentual de famílias que disseram não ter condições de pagar suas dívidas atrasadas ficou estável em 12,5% no mês, abaixo dos 13% registrados em setembro de 2025. Já a parcela de famílias consideradas muito endividadas caiu de 17,9% para 17,3%.

Apesar da melhora nesses indicadores, o tempo médio de atraso aumentou pelo segundo mês consecutivo. Em setembro, as dívidas estavam atrasadas, em média, por 65,3 dias, o maior período desde novembro de 2024, quando a média foi de 65,5 dias.

Além disso, 48,9% das dívidas em atraso estavam vencidas havia mais de 90 dias.

Para a economista Juliana Inhasz, professora do Insper, os dados mostram uma melhora ainda pequena no quadro de endividamento. Ela avalia que um dos fatores pode ser o comportamento da renda, em um mercado de trabalho que continua resiliente.

Segundo ela, a redução também pode ter alguma relação com programas de renegociação de dívidas, como o Deserola Brasil 2, que permitem reorganizar pagamentos e alongar os prazos.

A economista não vê a queda dos juros como a principal explicação para o movimento.

Mais famílias sem dívidas, mas orçamento segue pressionado

A pesquisa também mostra um aumento na parcela de famílias que não têm dívidas a vencer. O percentual passou de 17,4% em agosto para 18,1% em setembro.

Ao mesmo tempo, o comprometimento da renda continua elevado. Em média, as famílias destinam 29,6% da renda ao pagamento de dívidas. Para 19,4% delas, mais da metade da renda mensal está comprometida, maior percentual desde fevereiro, quando havia sido de 19,5%.

Outro movimento observado pela pesquisa foi o aumento da participação das dívidas com vencimento superior a um ano. Elas representaram 33,8% do total em setembro.

➡️ Na avaliação de Juliana, prazos mais longos podem ajudar a reduzir o peso das parcelas no orçamento no curto prazo, mas também prolongam o período em que a família permanece comprometida com a dívida.

A renegociação, portanto, pode aliviar a prestação mensal sem necessariamente significar que a dívida desapareceu.

Tabela mostra evolução do endividamento das familias brasileiras — Foto: g1

Inadimplência tem comportamento diferente conforme a renda, por que?

A diferença entre as faixas de renda aparece principalmente na inadimplência.

Entre as famílias que ganham até três salários mínimos, o percentual de inadimplentes caiu de 38,8% para 38,5%. Na faixa de três a cinco salários mínimos, passou de 28% para 27,8%.

Entre as famílias com renda de cinco a dez salários mínimos, a inadimplência teve uma pequena queda, de 20,3% para 20,2%.

Já entre aquelas que ganham mais de dez salários mínimos, o indicador subiu de 14,9% para 15%. Foi a única das quatro faixas analisadas pela pesquisa em que houve aumento da inadimplência.

Para Juliana, o movimento entre as famílias de maior renda não necessariamente significa deterioração financeira.

Uma possibilidade é que parte desses consumidores esteja escolhendo parcelar compras enquanto mantém o dinheiro aplicado, especialmente em investimentos de renda fixa, que seguem oferecendo retornos elevados.

“Pode fazer sentido manter o dinheiro investido e parcelar uma compra, em vez de sacar o dinheiro para pagar à vista.”

Ela ressalta que, nesse caso, o aumento da inadimplência pode estar relacionado mais à administração dos recursos do que a uma perda efetiva de capacidade de pagamento.

Crédito exige atenção, principalmente no orçamento apertado

Entre as famílias de menor renda, Juliana destaca que a previsibilidade da renda pode ser tão importante quanto o valor recebido.

Segundo ela, ter segurança de que o dinheiro entrará no fim do mês ajuda a organizar as despesas e definir quanto pode ser destinado ao pagamento de dívidas.

“Para quem tem renda mais baixa, o primeiro critério não deveria ser apenas o tamanho da renda, mas a certeza dessa renda.”

A economista também chama atenção para o uso do cartão de crédito. Para ela, o consumidor precisa considerar que o limite disponível não representa dinheiro adicional no orçamento.

“As pessoas precisam entender que o cartão de crédito não é uma extensão da renda.”

O mesmo cuidado vale para o parcelamento. Na avaliação de Juliana, ele faz mais sentido para bens que continuarão sendo usados durante o período de pagamento, como uma geladeira, do que para despesas consumidas rapidamente.

Parcelar compras do supermercado, por exemplo, pode criar compromissos para os meses seguintes sem que o consumidor ainda tenha o produto ou serviço correspondente àquela despesa.

“Quando você parcela um consumo imediato e cria passivos para os meses seguintes, fica mais difícil administrar o orçamento.”

Esse tipo de comportamento pode fazer com que uma dívida passe a pressionar o orçamento por vários meses e, em situações mais apertadas, leve o consumidor a recorrer novamente ao crédito para pagar compromissos anteriores.

articles.title: Ministro da Indústria aposta em superávit comercial de US$ 90 bilhões em 2026, acima da previsão oficial | G1
articles.standfirst: Apesar de reduzir a projeção para US$ 84,4 bilhões, governo ainda prevê o segundo maior saldo da série histórica; ministro afirma que resultado pode chegar a US$ 90 bilhões.
articles.summary: Apesar de reduzir a projeção para US$ 84,4 bilhões, governo ainda prevê o segundo maior saldo da série histórica; ministro afirma que resultado pode chegar a US$ 90 bilhões.
articles.body:
O Brasil deve registrar um superávit comercial de pelo menos US$ 90 bilhões (R$ 450 bilhões) em 2026, apesar da revisão para baixo da previsão oficial do governo , disse nesta quinta-feira (8) o ministro da Indústria, Comércio e Serviços, Márcio Elias Rosa.

O superávit comercial é o resultado positivo entre as exportações e as importações , quando o país vende mais ao exterior do que compra.

“Continuo apostando em US$ 90 bilhões, se não passar de US$ 90 bilhões”, afirmou o ministro a jornalistas na Federação das Indústrias do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (Firjan).

Na terça-feira (6), o Ministério do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços (MDIC) havia reduzido sua projeção para o saldo da balança comercial em 2026 de US$ 90 bilhões para US$ 84,4 bilhões (R$ 422 bilhões).

A revisão considera uma expectativa de crescimento menor das exportações e de desaceleração dos preços internacionais.

Mesmo com a redução da estimativa oficial, o saldo projetado pelo governo ainda seria 24% maior que o registrado em 2025, quando o Brasil teve superávit de US$ 68,1 bilhões (R$ 340,5 bilhões). Se confirmado, o resultado de 2026 seria o segundo maior da série histórica, atrás apenas do registrado em 2023.

Segundo Rosa, a estratégia do governo para sustentar as exportações é ampliar a presença dos produtos brasileiros em diferentes mercados.

A medida busca compensar os efeitos de fatores que dificultam as vendas para alguns destinos, como o aumento das tarifas impostas pelos Estados Unidos e o embargo da União Europeia à carne bovina e de aves brasileiras.

O ministro também afirmou que as negociações com os Estados Unidos para flexibilizar as tarifas estão avançando. Segundo ele, o governo brasileiro espera receber uma nova proposta americana dentro de três ou quatro semanas.

“Nós podemos constituir um grupo de trabalho, se for o caso, enquanto isso as equipes técnicas podem dialogar”, disse.

🔎 As tarifas são impostos cobrados sobre produtos importados. Quando um país aumenta essas taxas, os produtos estrangeiros ficam mais caros no mercado local, o que pode reduzir as vendas de outros países para aquele destino.

Márcio Elias Rosa, ministro do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços — Foto: GloboNews

articles.title: 'Split payment': mecanismo não prejudica caixa das empresas e garante redução da sonegação, diz Durigan  | G1
articles.standfirst: Na terça-feira (6), a coordenadora do núcleo econômico e porta-voz da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), Daniella Marques, afirmou que um eventual governo do PL pretende acabar com o mecanismo.
articles.summary: Na terça-feira (6), a coordenadora do núcleo econômico e porta-voz da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), Daniella Marques, afirmou que um eventual governo do PL pretende acabar com o mecanismo.
articles.body:
Dario Durigan — Foto: Washington Costa/MF

O ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, defendeu nesta quinta-feira (8) o chamado split payment, mecanismo criado pela reforma tributária que separa automaticamente, no momento da compra, o valor dos impostos do valor destinado ao vendedor.

"O slip payment é um instrumento tecnológico, uma inovação que foi incluída e debatida no Congresso e aprovada por ampla maioria, que garante a diminuição da sonegação. E não vai ter problema com o fluxo de caixa [das empresas]. Ele é um processo dialogado, sério e responsável", disse o ministro da Fazenda.

Em entrevista ao programa ALive, após ser questionada se acabaria com o "split payment", respondeu: "Claro que sim".

"Essa daí eu vou homenagear Carlos Bolsonaro [senador eleito pelo PL] e Adolfo Sacshida [economista que também faz parte da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro], que já pautaram esse governo, e foram muito vocais, foram implacáveis contra o 'split payment', que simplesmente asfixia o capital de giro do pequeno, que já está asfixiado", disse Daniella Marques.

Flávio Bolsonaro também falou na quarta-feira (7) sobre a intenção, se eleito, de mudar pontos da reforma tributária ( veja aqui ).

Previsto para ser obrigatório a partir de 2028, o "split payment" faz parte do novo sistema da Receita Federal para recolher os impostos sobre o consumo.

Com ele, o tributo poderá ser direcionado ao poder público no momento do pagamento, reduzindo o espaço para sonegação.

"As pequenas empresas não serão agora impactadas com a discussão do slip. Caso haja alguma dificuldade numa transição do pior sistema tributário do mundo, para um moderno e transparente, vai haver apoio do governo. Transições normativas adaptando o calendário de maneira que a gente não jogue fora ou prejudique o grande ganho do país que é a reforma tributária", afirmou Durigan.

Aprovada após 30 anos de debate, a reforma tributária busca manter a carga tributária atual, enquanto simplifica procedimentos, elimina distorções e institui o fim da cumulatividade (a chamada tributação em cascata).

No mês passado, cerca de 100 especialistas, acadêmicos, empresários e ex-autoridades da área econômica defenderam a reforma em uma carta-manifesto enviada aos candidatos à Presidência .

Entre eles, está Vanessa Canado, ex-assessora especial do Ministério da Economia para a reforma tributária durante o governo de Jair Bolsonaro.

"Atrasar, prejudicar de alguma maneira ou querer prorrogar a reforma tributária é prorrogar as decisões que o Congresso tomou, com o apoio técnico do Ministério da Fazenda. É importante atentar para o nível de insegurança, para o ambiente de negócio, e [evitar] gerar confusão", declarou o ministro.

De acordo com a Receita Federal, o "split payment" será obrigatório a partir de 2018 apenas nas operações entre empresas, o chamado "business to business" (B2B), ou seja, empresas que vendem para outras empresas.

As empresas do Simples Nacional, com faturamento anual de até R$ 4,8 milhões, puderam escolher entre permanecer no modelo simplificado atual ou migrar para um sistema híbrido, que permite o aproveitamento de créditos tributários.

A escolha para o primeiro semestre de 2027 foi feita em setembro, mas poderá ser alterada até o fim deste ano.

Já o microempreendedor individual (MEI) e o chamado nanoempreendedor permanecerão obrigatoriamente no Simples "puro", pois realizam vendas diretas ao consumidor final e não terão de recolher impostos pelo "split payment".

articles.title: Siará Tech Summit 2026 começa em Fortaleza reunindo ecossistema de inovação, tecnologia e negócios   | G1
articles.standfirst: Promovido pelo Sebrae/CE, evento segue até sexta-feira (9), no Centro de Eventos do Ceará, com expectativa de superar 50 mil inscritos e reunir 300 startups expositoras
articles.summary: Promovido pelo Sebrae/CE, evento segue até sexta-feira (9), no Centro de Eventos do Ceará, com expectativa de superar 50 mil inscritos e reunir 300 startups expositoras
articles.body:
Abertura oficial Siará Tech Summit 2026 — Foto: Sebrae/CE

O Siará Tech Summit 2026 teve início nesta quarta-feira (7), no Centro de Eventos do Ceará, em Fortaleza, reunindo empreendedores, startups, investidores, grandes empresas, universidades, representantes do poder público e instituições ligadas ao desenvolvimento econômico e à inovação. Promovido pelo Serviço de Apoio às Micro e Pequenas Empresas do Ceará (Sebrae/CE), o evento segue até sexta-feira (9), com programação voltada à tecnologia, aos novos negócios e às conexões entre diferentes atores do ecossistema de inovação.

Considerado o principal evento de inovação, tecnologia e negócios do Ceará e um dos maiores do segmento no Nordeste, o Siará Tech Summit chega à edição de 2026 com expectativa de superar 50 mil inscritos e reunir 300 startups expositoras. Ao longo dos três dias, o público terá acesso a palestras, painéis, mentorias, pitch sessions, rodadas de negócios, experiências imersivas, exposição de startups e espaços voltados à aproximação entre empreendedores, investidores e grandes empresas.

A solenidade de abertura contou com representantes de instituições públicas e privadas ligadas ao empreendedorismo, à inovação e ao desenvolvimento econômico. Participaram Fábio Krieger Lopes Reis, gerente da Unidade de Competitividade do Sebrae Nacional; José Cid Sousa Alves, presidente do Conselho Deliberativo Estadual do Sebrae Ceará; João Porto Guimarães, vice-presidente do Conselho Deliberativo Estadual do Sebrae Ceará; Joaquim Cartaxo Filho, diretor-superintendente do Sebrae Ceará; Alci Porto, diretor técnico do Sebrae Ceará; Reginaldo Braga, diretor de Administração e Finanças do Sebrae Ceará; Joélia Marques, pró-reitora do Instituto Federal de Educação, Ciência e Tecnologia do Ceará (IFCE); Eliane Brasil, superintendente estadual do Banco do Nordeste; André Montenegro, vice-presidente da Federação das Indústrias do Estado do Ceará (FIEC); Carlos Bezerra Filho, superintendente da Federação da Agricultura e Pecuária do Estado do Ceará (FAEC); Luiz Fernando Monteiro Bittencourt, presidente da Fecomércio Ceará; Cristian Tadeu, presidente da Softex; Artur Bruno, presidente do Instituto de Pesquisa e Planejamento de Fortaleza (Ipplan); e Fábio Feijó, secretário do Desenvolvimento Econômico do Estado do Ceará.

Para Fábio Krieger Lopes Reis, a capacidade de articulação entre diferentes setores é um dos principais ativos do evento. “O Sebrae Ceará vem realizando um trabalho de excelência. Quem está aqui está no lugar certo, em um ambiente que fomenta ideias, conexões e negócios e aproxima a cadeia produtiva dos ecossistemas e dos ambientes de inovação. É assim que vamos continuar promovendo o desenvolvimento”, afirmou.

Já Joaquim Cartaxo Filho destacou como o avanço do ecossistema cearense está ligado à capacidade de integrar diferentes territórios e instituições. “O Sebrae Ceará está construindo uma nova centralidade na rede de inovação do Nordeste e do Brasil, focada em conexão, conhecimento e capacidade de cooperação. A cada ano, o Ceará segue consolidando a criação de um polo de software voltado às demandas, vocações e talentos dos 184 municípios cearenses, conectados por meio do Ceará Habitats Digitais”, destacou.

Segundo Cartaxo, esse processo permite descentralizar as oportunidades e, ao mesmo tempo, aproximar inovação e necessidades concretas da população. “A tecnologia deve servir às pessoas e as pessoas devem orientar a tecnologia. Com um Ceará mais empreendedor, o Sebrae Ceará atua em rede com os governos estadual e municipais, universidades, organizações empresariais e comunitárias, empresas, investidores e a sociedade civil. Cada parceiro contribui com seus recursos e competências”, acrescentou.

A superintendente estadual do Banco do Nordeste, Eliane Brasil, ressaltou que a inovação também depende da criação de condições para que boas ideias se transformem em negócios. “Uma boa ideia precisa de crédito, de capital e de confiança para se transformar em empresa, em empreendimento e em resultado. O Banco do Nordeste tem a missão de ser esse elo, com recursos do FNE voltados à inovação, apoio às startups e aos ambientes de inovação e presença em todo o território nordestino”, afirmou.

Ela destacou ainda que o desenvolvimento tecnológico precisa produzir efeitos concretos para a sociedade. “A tecnologia, por si só, não desenvolve uma região. O que desenvolve é a tecnologia a serviço das pessoas, aquela que gera emprego, reduz desigualdades e leva produtividade ao agricultor familiar, ao comerciante e à cooperativa. Nosso compromisso é que nenhuma boa ideia, do sertão ao litoral, passando pela serra, fique na gaveta por falta de financiamento e oportunidade”, completou.

O vice-presidente da FIEC, André Montenegro, reforçou o papel da pesquisa e da inovação na transformação da economia. “Só se muda com muito trabalho, estudo, pesquisa e inovação. A necessidade é a mãe da inovação, e um evento como esse acende uma esperança de mudança. Empresas, governo, universidades e empreendedores precisam trabalhar juntos para que daqui saiam grandes negócios, inovação, novas empresas, renda e desenvolvimento”, pontuou.

A necessidade de acompanhar as transformações tecnológicas como parte fundamental para avanço da economia cearense foi destacada pelo presidente da Fecomércio Ceará, Luiz Fernando Monteiro Bittencourt. “No Sistema Fecomércio, a inovação é sempre priorizada porque precisamos estar atentos aos modelos de inteligência artificial que podem trazer benefícios para o comércio e manter nossas empresas atualizadas. Além da inteligência do nosso povo, nossa capacidade de união tem sido fundamental para a construção desse cenário de desenvolvimento do Estado”, afirmou.

Programação projetada para dar suporte às iniciativas tecnológicas no Ceará

A programação de 2026 está estruturada em seis grandes pilares: Internacionalização e Diplomacia da Inovação; Deep Tech e Inteligência Artificial; Inovação Governamental e Cidades do Futuro; Startups, Corporates e Negócios; Talentos, Educação e Inclusão; e Experiência e Cultura Digital. Ao longo dos três dias, o STS reúne palestras, painéis, mentorias, apresentações de startups, rodadas de negócios e outras atividades voltadas à troca de conhecimento e à geração de oportunidades.

O presidente da Softex, Cristian Tadeu, destacou a importância de ampliar o acesso à inovação para empresas de diferentes portes e setores. “O Sebrae exerce uma função essencial no desenvolvimento do Brasil porque entende que o empreendedorismo não acontece apenas nos grandes centros e não depende exclusivamente das grandes empresas. Ele está presente no pequeno negócio, na indústria local e regional, no campo, nos serviços, na economia criativa e, cada vez mais, nas empresas de base tecnológica”, disse.

A proposta de descentralização também foi ressaltada durante a cerimônia. O Siará Tech Summit busca fortalecer a articulação entre os diferentes ecossistemas de inovação do Ceará, aproximando demandas e potencialidades dos territórios de empreendedores, universidades, empresas e instituições públicas. Uma das ferramentas desse processo é o Ceará Habitats Digitais, plataforma criada para concentrar informações, conexões e oportunidades relacionadas à inovação em diferentes regiões do Estado.

Apoio institucional reforça relevância do evento

Representando a Prefeitura de Fortaleza, Artur Bruno, presidente do Ipplan, apontou oportunidades de desenvolvimento em diferentes áreas da economia local. “Temos a nossa economia azul, com possibilidades de desenvolvimento em muitas áreas, temos os empreendedores, as academias, universidades, sociedade civil e os governos federal, estadual e municipal. Em nome do prefeito Evandro Leitão, quero colocar a Prefeitura à disposição para promover o desenvolvimento sustentável da nossa cidade”, afirmou. “Como diz a sabedoria africana, quem quer chegar longe vai acompanhado”, acrescentou.

O secretário do Desenvolvimento Econômico do Estado, Fábio Feijó, reforçou a aposta do Governo do Ceará na tecnologia e no empreendedorismo. “O Governo do Ceará acredita na tecnologia e no empreendedorismo como motores do desenvolvimento do nosso Estado. Para nós, o Siará Tech Summit é um lugar onde se geram oportunidades para quem investe, pesquisa e trabalha para criar emprego e renda”, afirmou.

Feijó também destacou o peso dos pequenos negócios na economia cearense. “No Ceará, a força dos pequenos negócios é evidente. Já criamos mais de 115 mil pequenos negócios, que representam 97% das empresas formalizadas e mais de 60% dos empregos formais. Ao fomentar pequenos negócios de base tecnológica, conseguimos também impulsionar os resultados das grandes empresas. Por isso o Governo do Estado tem tanto interesse no ecossistema que vem sendo construído junto ao Siará Tech Summit”, acrescentou.

Na edição de 2025, o evento promoveu mais de 90 rodadas de negócios e gerou R$ 27 milhões em intenções de investimento. Para 2026, a proposta é ampliar as oportunidades de parceria e fortalecer o STS como ambiente de conexão entre startups, empresas, investidores, instituições de ensino e poder público.

O Siará Tech Summit segue até 9 de outubro, das 14h às 22h, no Centro de Eventos do Ceará, em Fortaleza.

articles.title: Chaves PIX ultrapassam 1 bilhão em setembro, revela Banco Central | G1
articles.standfirst: Números do BC mostram um crescimento de cerca de 80 milhões de chaves neste ano. Mais da metade das chaves são aleatórias. País somava 920 milhões de cadastros no fim de 2025.
articles.summary: As chaves PIX superaram 1 bilhão de cadastros no Banco Central, impulsionadas pelo uso de chaves aleatórias e um crescimento de 80 milhões apenas neste ano.
articles.body:
O número de chaves do PIX cadastradas no Banco Central ultrapassou a marca de 1 bilhão em setembro, segundo informações da autoridade monetária. Ao todo, eram 1,008 bilhão de chaves , ante 998 milhões em agosto.

Isso mostra um crescimento de cerca de 80 milhões de chaves neste ano, pois o total somava 920 milhões no fim de 2025.

Do total registrado em setembro, 956,7 milhões de chaves estavam ligadas a pessoas físicas e, o restante, 51,2 milhões , a pessoas jurídicas (empresas).

Com isso, a média de chaves por habitante no país se aproxima de cinco, visto que, a população brasileira estimada pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE) somou 214.211.951 habitantes no ano passado.

Dados da autoridade monetária mostram que mais da metade das chaves cadastradas ( 526 milhões ) são aleatórias.

Na sequência, aparecem os números de celular ( 166 milhões ), os CPFs ( 153 milhões ) e os endereços de e-mail ( 144,5 milhões ).

If you've been worried sick about higher prices, one of Wall Street's most-watched bulls has a message for you: relief may be on the way.

"I think the probabilities are really high. It's going to drop," Tom Lee, co-founder of Fundstrat Global Advisors, said of inflation in a Sept. 25 interview.

Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one

A single line on your car insurance policy could be inflating your premium by up to 30% — here's what to change

A record 45% of central banks plan to grow gold reserves — and many investors are following suit. Get your free gold IRA guide from Priority Gold

Lee was discussing inflation, bond yields and his outlook for the stock market on CNBC's (1) Closing Bell. He considers the next six months to be the most important for inflation.

If prices do come down, "this is not because of the Fed hikes," he said. "It's because of the policy that's already in place."

According to Lee, several things that pushed prices higher are starting to fade. These include tariffs, the cost of flash memory and stock market portfolio fees.

Lee pointed out that one reason inflation numbers could start to look better is that the government is changing the way it calculates inflation. This new methodology could knock the number down — from 3.4% to 3%.

So, with these factors in play, how does inflation come back?

Lee explained that a lot of things would have to go wrong. Home prices would have to climb higher, but he anticipates that higher rates will contain them. Memory prices would also have to surge again, and oil prices would have to make a move toward $150 a barrel.

"So I think the odds favor a much lower inflation year over year in six months," he said.

This is truly a bold call, especially considering the Federal Reserve's current stance and September interest rate hike — the first since 2023.

"The plain fact is that inflation is too high and has been for too long," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh (2) said during a press conference that followed the Sept. 16 Federal Open Market Committee meeting. "This summer's inflation readings do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved."

Scott Wapner, host of CNBC's Closing Bell , also pushed back in the interview with Lee, noting that changing how a number is calculated doesn't really change what people pay at the store.

articles.title: ‘Death by restriction’: As Trump sours H-1B visa dream, which Indian IT professionals face the biggest hit?
articles.summary: Indians, particularly IT sector professionals, hoping to work in the US, have a steep uphill climb.
articles.body: Indians, particularly IT sector professionals, hoping to work in the US, have a steep uphill climb. And, under the Donald Trump administration the fear is that the path may itself be lost! The repeated tightening of entry under the H-1B visa program is proof of the growing uncertainty.Three H-1B related changes are stacking on top of each other: the multiple $100,000 fee proposals, the wage-weighted lottery favoring more senior workers, new layoff and compliance scrutiny, and now the OPT/STEM-OPT $70,000 fee proposal for students looking to work in the US.And then there are statements from the Trump administration, hinting at doing away with the H-1B visa system itself. While admittedly, experts find that to be a far-fetched possibility, they do treat it as a symptom of the growing restrictions.Indians are the biggest beneficiaries of the H-1B visa programme, making up around 70% of the total approved list. Hence, it’s obvious that they would absorb the maximum impact of the immigration restrictions.The first consequence is the disruption to the traditional Indian pathway: Indian education gets you into an Indian IT company, which gets you an H-1B visa and US employment, and you get added to the green-card queue.That pathway is set to become much narrower or worse may even disappear!H-1B visas: What is happening?Experts say H-1B visas are an indication of the larger crackdown to ensure Americans don’t lose out on jobs.Rajiv Dabhadkar, Founder, National Organization For Software and Technology Professionals makes an important point: what is happening is not a visa system overhaul, it’s a deeper labour market problem from the US government perspective.“The US government is increasingly looking not only at the worker but at the entire employment chain,” he tells TOI.That means asking:Who sponsored the worker? Who actually employs and controls the worker? Where does the worker actually work? What wage is being paid? Was the worker recruited for a genuine job? Is an intermediary taking a margin between the employer and the worker? Was an American worker displaced? Was a qualified American worker given a genuine opportunity to compete for the position?“There is an older but highly relevant principle here. The 2010 Neufeld memorandum placed emphasis on the employer's “right to control” an H-1B beneficiary - essentially, who determines when, where and how the worker performs the job. That principle is particularly relevant when examining third-party staffing and intermediary arrangements,” Dabhadkar says.“This matters because the H-1B worker can actually be a victim of the same system that potentially disadvantages the American worker. The DOL OIG's investigation specifically refers to foreign workers being exploited through wage kickbacks and coercive arrangements, while also referring to below-wage labour undercutting American workers,” he adds.Indian IT professionals to be hit hardestIndian-born professionals continued to dominate the H-1B programme in FY 2025. The US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) approved 406,348 H-1B petitions, of which 283,772, or approximately 70%, were for beneficiaries born in India.Technology-related occupations were the largest category across the H-1B programme overall. Computer-related roles accounted for 252,088 approvals, or 62% of all beneficiaries. Systems analysis and programming was the largest detailed occupation, representing 50.4% of approvals.According to Akhil Chandna, Partner and Global People Solutions Leader, Grant Thornton Bharat, these figures point to sustained demand for technology skills, although USCIS does not publish a combined breakdown showing occupations specifically for Indian-born beneficiaries.As Xiao Wang, CEO, Boundless Immigration notes: A typical Indian H-1B holder is a computer and IT professional; the main beneficiaries are software developers, systems analysts, programmers, and IT consultants.Indian nationals took about 70% of all approved H-1B petitions last year, and IT workers were over 65% of H-1Bs over the past 5 years!The median annual compensation for all approved H-1B beneficiaries in FY 2025 was around $133,000, with median computer-specific roles at $140,000.But, as Wang says: the range is large - $117,000 at the 25th percentile and $179,000 at the 75th.According to the Boundless Immigration CEO, the impact for Indians is split across various job levels.For example, senior and highly paid Indian engineers at US tech firms are relatively insulated, and the wage-weighting actually favors them.But, early-career Indian workers and the IT-services staffing model are the ones squeezed hard, because that model runs on volume at lower wage levels, which is precisely what both the flat fee and the wage-weighting penalize.As Akhil Chandna points out, the H-1B programme continues to be driven largely by demand for technology talent, and it’s a trend that is only expected to accelerate with the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence and emerging technologies.“Against this backdrop, recent policy changes appear less focused on reducing H-1B numbers and more on reshaping the programme to attract highly skilled, higher-paid talent while strengthening safeguards for the US workforce,” he tells TOI.The bottom line is that litigation is now becoming a recurring feature of the immigration system.The $100,000 H-1B fee has been blocked by two federal judges, with business groups and other organizations challenging the administration's authority and implementation.In summary, the issue is not simply that one visa is becoming harder. The larger problem is systemic uncertainty across multiple legal pathways.What Indian IT companies could doAccording to a recent report, H-1B visa registrations by TCS, Infosys, HCLTech, Wipro, LTM and Tech Mahindra plunged 92% for FY27 to 1,763 from 21,919 a year earlier.The fall is far steeper than at major US employers, pointing to a structural shift in how Indian technology companies deploy talent in America.The shift is therefore already visible and further acceleration is likely.The top seven Indian firms won a little under 5,000 initial H-1B approvals in the most recent cycle, down roughly 70% from FY2015 and 37% from FY2024.“The main trend is that the body-shop model of flying Indian IT consultants to the client in the US model is gone, and it's being replaced by a mix of US local hiring for client-facing work and a much bigger offshore footprint in India for everything else. The crackdown speeds up a transition the economics were already driving,” Xiao Wang tells TOI.According to Rajiv Dabhadkar, the traditional model was: India employee + H-1B + US client site + onsite deliveryThe emerging model is increasingly: US local employee + India-based engineering/delivery team + global technology platformsH-1B visas: What are the alternatives?Xiao Wang does not see the H-1B visa programme being scrapped, despite the noise around it.“No administration can unilaterally scrap H-1B. It's written into statute (the Immigration and Nationality Act), so abolishing it takes an act of Congress. What's actually happening is death by restriction, making it more expensive and harder to get,” he tells TOI.Experts say alternative US visa options remain available for certain professionals, including the L-1 visa for intra-company transfers, the O-1 visa for individuals with extraordinary ability, and, in limited cases, employment-based green card pathways. These routes, however, typically have narrower eligibility requirements than the H-1B.But, while alternatives exist, getting them is not straightforward or easy.Rajiv Dabhadkar says L-1 and O-1 are not straightforward H-1B substitutes: L-1 is limited to qualifying intracompany transfers, while O-1 requires extraordinary ability and has a much higher evidence threshold.EB-1 is similarly highly selective, while EB-2 and EB-3 face a major India-specific obstacle: long green-card backlogs, he notes. All available FY2026 EB-2 immigrant visas for India had also been exhausted before the fiscal year ended, he adds.“It is tempting to say that if H-1B becomes unavailable, Indian professionals can simply move to another US visa category. That is not a realistic description of the current system. The alternatives exist legally, but for a large population of Indian professionals they are not scalable substitutes for H-1B,” says Rajiv Dabhadkar.Akhil Chandna says that beyond the US, countries such as Canada, the UK, Australia, Germany, Singapore and the UAE continue to attract skilled Indian professionals through a range of work and residence programmes.The unexpected advantage for IndiaNot all will be lost, though. In fact, India may stand to benefit.There is the possibility of remote working, which in turn would create jobs in India.“Work that can be performed remotely, such as software development, testing and support services, may increasingly be delivered from India and other global delivery centres,” says Akhil Chandna.He also believes that a complete shift away from H-1B sponsorship is unlikely.“US businesses will continue to need specialized talent on the ground for project leadership, client engagement and complex technology implementations. The more likely outcome is a balanced approach: stronger local hiring in the US, selective H-1B sponsorship for critical skills, and expanded offshore delivery for roles that do not require physical presence,” he tells TOI.Rajiv Dabhadkar explains how this helps: it would mean more engineering in India; more Global Capability Centres; more AI and data science work in India; more product development in India; more cloud and cybersecurity engineering in India; more remote delivery; more US local hiring for customer-facing roles.“This creates a potentially unexpected outcome. H-1B restrictions could simultaneously produce: more American hiring and more high-value employment in India. That is why I don't see the future simply as "Indian IT loses because of H-1B restrictions." The business model is being redesigned,” he concludes.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Supreme Court call to reduce drug prices puts focus on scope and extent of mark ups
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court’s call for a cap on trade margins, after flagging huge mark-ups on essential medicines, has brought into focus the scope of
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court’s call for a cap on trade margins, after flagging huge mark-ups on essential medicines, has brought into focus the scope of such a move and what constitutes a reasonable mark-up across the distribution and trade channels. The pharma industry, while broadly supportive of rationalising margins, is of the view that they be imposed only on medicines priced at Rs 100 or more per unit, sources told TOI.Labelling it as "carnage", the apex court recently said the gap between price to retailer (PTR) and MRP of medicines billed to patients is 10x, particularly on cancer medicines. The SC bench was hearing petitions concerning regulation of medicine prices, generic prescriptions and controls on medical devices under the Drugs (Prices Control) Order (DPCO), 2013."Industry is in favour of rationalising trade margins, but the framework has to recognise the different costs at each stage of the distribution chain, especially for cancer and hospital injectables. We had communicated that margins should not be imposed on low priced medicines, particularly those under Rs 100 per unit. Capping trade margins has been under discussion for a long time, with multiple rounds of consultations earlier", an industry expert said.Another issue which has wide ramifications for industry is SC’s urge that trade margins be capped at 16% on all medicines, and not just on scheduled or essential drugs.At present, ceiling prices are fixed by the drug price regulator, NPPA, on 3,482 medicines, with a built-in 16% retailer margin, but this is only on scheduled drugs. These represent roughly about 18% of the Rs 3 lakh crore domestic pharma retail market.The balance-- non-scheduled formulations-- face no caps, with companies free to decide the mark up. This category of drugs is allowed a 10% price increase as per policy."It has been noticed that some of the launch prices of new drugs are completely unjustified, and this is where trade margins need to be brought in”, an industry observer said.Further, the chemist body, AIOCD says a rational trade margin of 10% for wholesalers/stockists and 20% for retailers should be in place for all medicines, "to prevent artificial MRP inflation and unfair discounting.""A moderately high MRP is not necessarily unreasonable, as manufacturers have legitimate costs to consider. However, if MRP is deliberately kept high to facilitate large discounts or deep discounting, it can mislead consumers and distort competition," Rajiv Singhal, general secretary AIOCD, told TOI.He added that NPPA should therefore examine the entire distribution chain to see where the issue lies.Further, for cancer and high-priced medicines which have been under the spotlight, a section of the industry feels that these may need cold-chain storage, specialised handling and trained administration, and therefore, any assessment should consider the entire transaction chain.This comes even as recently the Kerala high court expressed concern on exorbitantly priced patented cancer medicines, and Karnataka also flagged the 10 to 52x markup on cancer drugs and consumables, seeking the Centre’s intervention.You use AI every day. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Air India and Air India Express hiked fuel surcharg on Thursday for both International and domestic flights while Akasa Air announced its decision to re-introduced the surcharge."ATF prices have witnessed significant volatility in recent months, driven largely by geopolitical developments and sustained pressure on global energy markets. The latest increase in fuel prices has further elevated operating costs for airlines, with fuel continuing to account for a substantial proportion of overall airline expenditure," said the airlines in a statement."The revised fuel surcharge will be reflected in the fare applicable to new bookings made from 0000 Hrs IST on 9 October for Air India Express, and from 1100 hrs IST on 9 October for Air India. The surcharge varies by sector and route category," it added.For domestic one-way flights, the surcharge ranges from Rs 400 to Rs 1,200, while international surcharges range from $55 for West Asia/Middle East to $215 for North America.Meanwhile, Akasa Air will reintroduce fuel surcharges on domestic flights and increase the levy on international services from October 9, citing sustained higher Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) prices amid geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. The domestic surcharge will range from Rs 375 to Rs 1,150 depending on distance, while the surcharge on international flights will be Rs 2,500; the airline had introduced the levy in March but later withdrew it on domestic services. (Bloomberg) -- Chipotle Mexican Grill Inc. ( CMG ) shares jumped after the Financial Times reported that Starbucks Corp. has worked with advisers in recent months on a takeover proposal for the burrito chain.

The status of the takeover plans couldn't be immediately learned and a mega deal of this size might never get off the ground, the Times said, citing people familiar with the matter. Brian Niccol, Starbucks' chief executive officer since 2024, previously was the top executive at Chipotle.

Shares of Chipotle surged as much as 8.6% in New York trading on Thursday. Starbucks declined as much as 6.7%, the most intraday in more than a year.

articles.title: IRS issues notices for a $1,000 retirement match. Here's who qualifies.
articles.summary: The Saver's Match program could add up to $1,000 a year to eligible taxpayers' retirement savings starting in 2027.
articles.body:

The Internal Revenue Service is issuing notices to taxpayers stating that they may qualify for the Saver's Match, a government-funded $1,000 retirement account contribution, beginning in 2027. The program replaces the Saver's Credit, which ends on Dec. 31, 2026.

Taxpayers who previously filed for that credit are receiving a notification about the new program, which will provide a matching contribution of up to $1,000 for single filers and $2,000 for joint filers in the 2027 tax year.

The Saver's Match was created by the bipartisan SECURE 2.0 Act, which was signed into law in 2022.

"Beginning in 2027, the government will match 50% of eligible retirement contributions, up to $1,000 per person," said Brandon M. Cox, founder of Coastline Complete Wealth in Bluffton, S.C. "A married couple could receive double that, or $2,000. Unlike the current Saver's Credit, this money will go directly into a retirement account rather than simply reducing someone's tax bill."

That's a 50% boost to retirement savings, Cox added.

The Saver's Match also doesn't count against your retirement account contribution limit, said Greg Black, founder and senior wealth advisor of Tencap Wealth Coaching in Utah.

"You contribute the full amount into your IRA, plus still get the extra $1,000." And it's not a one-time match, he noted. "If you contribute $2,000 and get a 50% match, that's $1,000 of free money going into your account every single year, as long as your income fits inside those limits."

The IRS says taxpayers may qualify for the 50% match of retirement plan contributions if they:

Contribute to a retirement plan or IRA (there is no minimum contribution amount)

Are not claimed as a dependent on another person's return

The program targets households with modest incomes — "people who owe little or no federal income tax," Cox said. "Many lower-income Americans couldn't benefit from the old Saver's Credit because they didn't owe enough in taxes. Now they can."

Here's an example of how the Saver's Match works: A single tax filer, earning $19,000, contributing $1,500 to an IRA, would receive the full 50% match of $750. The Saver's Match income limits are shown below.

Saver's Match rates based on filing status and modified adjusted gross income

Married filing jointly, qualifying surviving spouse

Income limits will be adjusted for inflation in years after 2027

Even if taxpayers haven't filed for the previously offered Saver's Credit — and didn't receive the notice — they can claim the Saver's Match when filing their 2027 federal tax return in 2028, if they qualify. A new Form 8880-A will be available.

The match cannot be made in a Roth IRA, Black said; only traditional IRAs, 401(k), and 403(b) plans will be eligible. The IRS is still developing guidance on how it will deliver payments to employer-sponsored retirement plans, such as 401(k)s.

A new website, TrumpIRA.gov , debuting on Jan. 1, 2027, will provide access to low-cost IRA plans for those without a current account. Taxpayers don't have to open an IRA at the government-sponsored website to get the match, Black said.

"It's more of a marketplace or a portal that points people towards qualifying IRAs. There are plenty of low-cost IRA options out there. There are custodians who have no custodial fee. And there are low-cost ETFs and mutual funds people can invest in inside those IRAs."

Cox said that taxpayers should also be aware of the timing of the retirement plan matches.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Trump administration has stepped up its crackdown on the US immigration system, suspending major technology companies including Cognizant,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Trump administration has stepped up its crackdown on the US immigration system, suspending major technology companies including Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, Capgemini and HCL from the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme amid allegations of abuse of H-1B visas and the employment of foreign workers.US Vice President JD Vance accused Microsoft of laying off thousands of American workers while simultaneously benefiting from thousands of H-1B visas and green cards. The administration has also put nine universities under investigation over alleged misuse of visa-related programmes, adding to growing uncertainty for foreign workers and international students in the US.Announcing Microsoft's suspension from the PERM programme, Vance said the company had laid off 6,000 American workers while benefiting from 6,300 H-1B visas and nearly 3,000 green cards."There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused the system more than Microsoft."“If you do the math, for every worker that Microsoft laid off, they replaced that worker with one and a half foreign indentured servants,” Vance said at a White House news conference.Vance also accused companies of using foreign workers to undercut American employees, saying: "This is a fundamental INSULT to the American worker and to the American way of life. We CANNOT allow visa programs that were designed to ensure that American corporations had access to the best and the brightest, to use them to undercut the wages of American workers!"What is the PERM programmeThe Permanent Labour Certification programme, or PERM, is a Department of Labour process that allows US employers to seek certification to permanently employ foreign workers.Under the process, employers generally have to demonstrate that there are not enough able, willing, qualified and available US workers for the job and that hiring a foreign worker will not adversely affect the wages and working conditions of similarly employed American workers.Once the labour certification is approved by the Department of Labour, the employer can proceed with an immigrant petition to the US Citizenship and Immigration Services, generally through Form I-140.For H-1B workers, PERM can therefore form an important step in the employment-based green card process. Suspending a company's access to the programme can make it harder for the company to sponsor eligible foreign workers for permanent residence.How PERM was meant to protect US workersThe PERM programme is designed to ensure that American workers are not disadvantaged when employers seek to hire foreign workers for permanent jobs. Before sponsoring a foreign worker for a green card, an employer generally has to demonstrate that there are not enough qualified, willing and available US workers for the position and that hiring the foreign worker will not adversely affect the wages and working conditions of similarly employed Americans.The concern for US authorities arises when employers manipulate or bypass this labour-market test. Fraudulent recruitment can make it appear that no suitable American worker is available when, in reality, qualified US workers may have been discouraged from applying or effectively excluded from consideration. The Department of Labor's inspector general has identified vulnerabilities in the PERM system, including concerns over fraudulent applications, inadequate supporting documentation and weaknesses in post-certification enforcement.Wages are another concern. Employers are required to meet prevailing wage requirements, which are intended to prevent foreign-worker hiring from depressing wages for American workers in comparable jobs. If employers circumvent these requirements or use arrangements that effectively reduce the foreign worker's compensation, the government says the system can undermine the safeguards built into PERM.The administration's latest moves have also extended beyond companies. The Department of Homeland Security has proposed a $70,000 fee for international students participating in the Optional Practical Training programme, which allows eligible foreign students to work in jobs related to their studies.You use AI every day. articles.title: Gas prices face new threat as Hurricane Isaias forces widespread Gulf oil shutdowns
articles.summary: Hurricane Isaias threatens to disrupt U.S. oil and gasoline production at a moment when retail gas and diesel prices are squeezing American consumers.
articles.body: A powerful storm snaking its way through the Gulf of Mexico threatens to disrupt U.S. oil and gasoline production at a moment when retail gas and diesel prices are squeezing American consumers and companies. Hurricane Isaias is rapidly intensifying and expected to make landfall along the northeastern Gulf shore late Friday or early Saturday. Already, major oil companies, including Chevron and Shell, have begun shutting down some oil production sites. Chevron said it was shutting down four of its assets in the Gulf, although production at its five other facilities in the region remained at normal levels. Shell said it was halting production at five sites. All told, nearly two-thirds of Gulf oil production and 57% of natural gas production had been shut in by noon Thursday, according to the U.S. Marine Minerals Administration. Hurricanes and major storms are common in the region, so oil companies have well-established evacuation and shutdown protocols. Still, the timing could hardly be worse for U.S. consumers. The U.S.-Israeli war against Iran has spawned broader regional conflict, which continues to disrupt energy supplies and drive oil and gasoline prices higher. Global benchmark Brent crude oil prices surged nearly 5% in early Thursday trading amid reports that President Donald Trump was considering renewed attacks against Iran. U.S. gasoline prices averaged $4.36, down slightly from a week ago but still up 21 cents over the past month. “This could not have come at a worse time as gasoline and diesel inventories are quite low,” Andy Lipow, president of Lipow Oil Associates LLC consultancy, wrote in a note Wednesday. Nearly all U.S. offshore production is in Isaias’ path, he wrote, which means “the impact, even short-lived, can be significant.” Lipow estimated that 14% of the nation’s refining capacity is in the storm’s path. Given that most U.S. refineries are now running at maximum levels in response to the global squeeze on capacity, “There is no slack in the system,” he wrote. Oil is a globally traded commodity, so any reduction in supplies will send prices higher around the world. Refineries in the path of Isaias are likely to see flooding that could take them offline for up to 10 days, said Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy. That is expected to produce a short-term squeeze for U.S. gasoline prices. But for U.S. motorists, the bigger concerns remain overseas — especially in Russia, where Ukraine continues to target refineries. “The refining problem is looking like, short to medium term, at least three to six months,” De Haan said. “And it sounds like it’s going to be continuing, especially with Ukraine promising to target more Russian refineries. So there needs to be some de-escalation there for there to be any relief, but it doesn’t look like we’re seeing it.”

articles.title: Grandmother and her son gifted 2.5-acre land to his second wife, who sold it; his daughter from first marriage claimed it was ancestral, but Madras HC rejects her plea
articles.summary: Land disputes are a tricky matter especially when it comes to property that one person claims is ancestral, and the other as self-acquired.
articles.body: Land disputes are a tricky matter especially when it comes to property that one person claims is ancestral, and the other as self-acquired.In one such case, a daughter has claimed share in a property that her grandmother and father gifted to her stepmother. The Madras High Court has ruled against her claim.What the case is aboutIn this case, a man who owned 2.5 acres of land executed a Will in1953, leaving the property to his wife, for her lifetime. The Will, however, placed a restriction on her rights. She could neither sell the land nor transfer it to anyone else because the property was ultimately intended to pass to their son.Also Read | US-based daughter files case against parents seeking share in properties; Karnataka HC rejects her ‘ancestral’ claim, saying they were father's separate assets, not coparcenary propertyThe man did not transfer the land directly to the son because he was still young and, at that stage, was considered incapable of handling the property responsibly. The son eventually married twice and had five children.When the question of ownership of the 2.5-acre property arose, the son and his mother jointly executed a gift settlement deed in 1975. Through the deed, they transferred the entire property to the son’s second wife.Despite the transfer, the man continued to reside on the property and remained in possession of the land until his death in 1986, according to an ET report.A decade later, in 1996, the man’s second wife sold the 2.5-acre property to an outsider. The sale prompted opposition from the man’s daughter from his first marriage. She claimed that her stepmother had no authority to sell the land because, according to her, the property was ancestral and therefore she was entitled to a share in it.The daughter subsequently approached the court, arguing that her father had owned 2.5 acres of ancestral property and that her stepmother had unlawfully sold it. After a prolonged legal battle, the Madras High Court rejected her case on September 8, 2026.Also Read | Retired bank employee got Rs 12.27 lakh leave encashment and claimed Rs 3 lakh exemption in 2020, but government later hiked limit to Rs 25 lakh in 2023; ITAT Chennai allows full tax exemptionWhy did the granddaughter lose the case?The Madras High Court held that the property was not ancestral but self-acquired. As a result, under Hindu law, the man and his mother were legally entitled to execute the gift settlement deed in favour of the man’s second wife, who could subsequently sell the property. The court held that Section 14(2) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, was applicable to the case.Section 14(1) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, deals with situations where a Hindu woman receives property in recognition of a right or claim to maintenance.In such circumstances, the law treats her interest in the property as ownership. Section 14(2), on the other hand, applies where a Hindu individual acquires property through instruments such as a gift deed or Will and the transfer is made without it being linked to a claim for maintenance or other conditions, the ET report said.In this case, the Madras High Court concluded that Section 14(2) applied because the life interest granted under the Will was not provided in lieu of maintenance. The Will had separately made provisions for her maintenance. Therefore, the life interest created in her favour did not become an absolute estate under Section 14(1).Also Read | Housing society wanted to label Mumbai doctor a defaulter over Rs 1.42 lakh maintenance dues and 18% interest; why Maharashtra court has granted him interim protectionIn deciding the nature of the 2.5-acre land, the Madras High Court referred to the Supreme Court's judgment in C.N. Arunachala Mudaliar vs C.A. Muruganatha Mudaliar, reported in AIR 1953 SC 495. The Supreme Court had held that the character of property is determined by the intention of the person who creates the Will.In other words, where a Will gives property to a beneficiary for his absolute enjoyment, the property is treated as separate or self-acquired property. However, if the intention behind the Will is to partition the property or to preserve it for the benefit not only of the beneficiary but also his legal heirs, the property would be considered joint family ancestral property.Applying this principle, the Madras High Court held that the 2.5-acre land became the separate property of the father because the grandfather’s Will showed an intention that the property would ultimately pass to his son.Adnan Siddiqui, Partner at King Stubb and Kasiva, told ET that the outcome rested on three key findings by the High Court, all of which went against the granddaughter.The first was the court's conclusion that the land was the self-acquired property of her grandfather and not ancestral property. This was significant because both the granddaughter and her stepmother had stated the same position in their respective evidence.Since the property was self-acquired, the grandfather was free to dispose of it through his Will. The court interpreted the Will as having transferred the property absolutely to his son in his individual capacity.The second finding concerned the interest given to the grandmother under the Will. Although she received only a life interest and was specifically not given the right to sell the property, the court held that she and her son could jointly deal with the property as the life-estate holder and remainderman when there was no other person with an interest in it. They exercised that right by executing the 1975 settlement deed in favour of the second wife.The third factor was that the granddaughter herself acknowledged that the settlement deed had been executed. There was also no material on record to establish that her father had ever challenged the deed during the 11 years he lived after it was executed. Since his widow and daughter derived their claim through the man, they could not challenge an act that he himself had not disputed.The High Court also accepted that the second wife’s marriage had been established, while specifically leaving the question of its legal validity open. The second wife subsequently sold the property in 1996, and the court also upheld that transaction.Once the court upheld the validity of the gift settlement deed, the subsequent sale of the 2.5-acre property was also held to be valid.Also Read | 83-year-old woman got Rs 12.28 lakh after son’s death, but sought Rs 15,000 maintenance from college-going granddaughter and a share of family pension from son’s widow; Kerala HC rejects both claimsYou use AI every day. articles.title: Amazon India lays off 130 employees; 400 affected in three rounds this yr
articles.summary: Amazon India lays off 130 in third round this year, taking total to about 400; retail, Stores and customer service roles affected, with severance offered.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Amazon India carried out a fresh round of layoffs, its third this year, affecting around 130 employees in its retail and stores business and customer service, sources told TOI. Amazon’s Stores business spans its core retail operations, online marketplace, and technology and tools that support sellers. The latest cuts are understood to have also affected teams in its selling partner services (SPS) division. Employees in the L2-L4 bands, comprising junior- to mid-level roles, are among those affected.The latest round brings the total number of employees laid off by the company in India since the beginning of the year to around 400, sources said. A majority of the 1,000 employees affected in the latest global round were based in the US and the UK. A year ago, Amazon’s global restructuring also extended to its India operations, impacting an estimated 1,000-1,500 employees.Some employees reportedly received connect emails involving L7/L8 (senior) employees, while several of those affected are managers and L4 employees. The connect email asks employees to “prioritize the meeting and join in person” and says, “We will discuss the agenda and the purpose of the meeting during our connect.”The layoffs are being driven by factors including job-family mix, location and co-location, and management structure, rather than being applied uniformly across the organisation.When TOI reached out to Amazon, its spokesperson said, “We’ve adjusted parts of our Stores business because we believe this structure will better enable us to deliver on our priorities. As part of these changes, we’ve made the difficult decision to eliminate a small number of roles, and we’re committed to supporting affected employees through their transition.”The severance package for affected employees is understood to include one month’s salary for every year of service, along with three months’ salary, leave encashment, outplacement services and continuation of insurance coverage until the next renewal cycle.Sources told TOI that two key criteria were considered. One was hub location and co-location, with employees expected to be based in designated company hubs and more than 85% of a team expected to be co-located with its manager. The span of control was another factor, with managers expected to have at least seven direct reports and managers of managers at least six. The aim is also to avoid excessive management layers or “nesting”, where employees at the same level report to one another.They also told TOI that the company is evaluating higher unregretted attrition (URA) targets. At Amazon, URA refers to employees the company considers it is willing to lose, whether through voluntary exits or performance-management processes.Amazon India to discontinue salary advance programme from Dec 1Separately, Amazon India has told employees it will discontinue its salary advance (SA) programme from Dec 1, replacing it with Anytime Pay (ATP) for blue-badge, or permanent, employees. Under ATP, employees can access wages they have already earned, with 24/7 access, instant bank transfers and unlimited withdrawals between the 1st and 23rd of each month. Amazon said the move is aimed at simplifying its pay practices and aligning them with global standards.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Meta bulls have a new Muse stat to love. Amazon could spoil it.
articles.summary: It's still up and to the right for Meta Muse despite a few new stumbling blocks.
articles.body:
The meteoric rise of Meta's ( META ) new Muse AI agent looks to be continuing despite a few new stumbling blocks.

Daily active users for Muse keep climbing , hitting 2.182 million on Oct. 5, according to new data from Similarweb. Usage has risen steadily throughout October.

The increase may help soothe some concerns as Muse has reportedly hit a new hurdle: websites — Amazon ( AMZN ) being the top-of-mind example — blocking AI agents from browsing or completing purchases.

If Muse's usefulness becomes limited as more websites treat AI agents as bots or security risks, that could dent the new bullish case for the stock that has developed since the agent's September launch.

Meta stock is down 7.7% from its record high reached in late September amid the Muse hype.

The hype on Muse has been very real, to say the least

Deutsche Bank analyst Benjamin Black sees Muse reaching up to 8% of Meta's revenue by 2030, which nets out to roughly $36 billion in sales for the product. On the lower end of the prediction scale, Black sees Muse pulling in sales of $2.4 billion by 2030.

"In our view, Meta found a clear gap amongst current AI-agentic offerings — at the intersection of mobile app-based ecosystem, with a consumer-oriented UI which is seamless to use, the ability to complete transactions autonomously, free-to-use for the most part, and always-on feature within its own virtual machine — that makes it the service virtually unique in today's market," Black said.

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show and the Power Players with Brian Sozzi podcast, and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team. articles.title: Major crackdown on Green Cards: What is PERM program & which IT firms has US suspended
articles.summary: The US has suspended eight major technology companies, including Microsoft, Tata, Infosys and Wipro, from the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM)
articles.body: The US has suspended eight major technology companies, including Microsoft, Tata, Infosys and Wipro, from the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme, in a major crackdown on the use of foreign workers for jobs that the government says could be filled by Americans. The move was announced by Vice President JD Vance, Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling and Attorney General Todd Blanche under the US Anti-Fraud Task Force.The Department of Labour said it would not accept new or process pending PERM applications involving the companies. Sonderling said the firms alone had requested almost three million foreign workers since 2009, securing more than 230,000 H-1B visa approvals and over 100,000 permanent labour certifications.Vance singled out Microsoft, accusing it of laying off 6,000 American workers in 2025 while obtaining more than 6,000 H-1B approvals and filing 3,682 PERM applications. "Microsoft laid off 6,000 American workers in 2025 after certifying that it could not find qualified American employees," Vance said.Which IT firms are suspended from PERM programme:MicrosoftAdobeCognizantInfosysTataWiproHCLCapgeminiSonderling said the suspensions covered some of the world's largest IT outsourcing companies. He said Microsoft and Adobe were being suspended due to multiple active federal investigations, while the other firms were also targeted as part of the broader crackdown.Indian professionals account for more than 70% of approved H-1B petitions annually, making the move particularly significant for Indian technology workers seeking permanent residency in the US.What is PERM visa and how does it work?PERM, or Permanent Labour Certification, is not itself a visa. It is a labour certification process administered by the US Department of Labour that is required for most employment-based green card applications.Under the system, a US employer must establish that there are not enough qualified, willing and available American workers for a particular job, and that hiring a foreign worker will not adversely affect the wages and working conditions of similarly employed US workers.The process generally begins with the employer identifying a permanent, full-time position and determining its minimum requirements and duties. The employer then obtains a prevailing wage determination from the Department of Labour.The employer must also complete the required recruitment and notification process to demonstrate that it has sought qualified US workers. After completing these steps, it submits the PERM application to the Department of Labour, usually through the online FLAG system. If the labour certification is approved, the employer can use it as a step towards filing the relevant employment-based immigrant petition with US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS).You use AI every day.
